design_question: A first-time visitor should know where to arrive, what to see, how long each route takes, where to rest, and how to continue without a smartphone.
design_answer: Turn the green spine into a legible sequence of arrival, memory, everyday life, AI demonstration, and return. Every digital enhancement has a paper, physical-signage, and human-service fallback.
boundary_note: All route geometry and distances are conceptual targets drawn inside the submitted provisional boundary. They are not surveyed walking measurements, official access points, or engineering alignments.

arrival_options.experience: A visible welcome flag, large-print paper map, tactile route strip, toilets, water, and a staffed orientation desk are available before the visitor chooses a route.
arrival_options.pending: Exact station interface and step-free engineering require official transport and accessibility review.

arrival_options.mode_zh: 出租车/网约车临时下客
arrival_options.experience: A short-stay drop-off is separated from the walking spine. A person can be dropped close to the welcome desk without crossing the main cycle path.
arrival_options.pending: Curb geometry, traffic management, and parking supply require professional confirmation.

arrival_options.experience: A staffed bicycle park, pump, repair shelf, and clear pedestrian dismount line sit beside the welcome desk.
arrival_options.pending: Capacity and operating responsibility are design targets, not commitments.

visitor_nodes.highlight: The first 10 minutes: orient, choose a route, store a bicycle, use the toilet, and meet a person.
visitor_nodes.no_app_fallback: A paper route card uses color, number, and landmark icons; no QR code is required.
visitor_nodes.visitor_problem_solved: I do not know where the public entrance is or what I can do in two hours.

visitor_nodes.highlight: A 3-minute human briefing offers a short route, half-day route, quiet route, family route, and rainy-day alternative.
visitor_nodes.no_app_fallback: The route card is stamped at physical nodes; optional digital narration is never the only information channel.
visitor_nodes.visitor_problem_solved: I do not want to download an app or share identity data before entering.

visitor_nodes.highlight: The historic railway story begins with a physical timeline, shade, model fragments, and a short audio/large-print explanation.
visitor_nodes.no_app_fallback: Every story panel has a short printed version and a human explanation point.
visitor_nodes.visitor_problem_solved: I want to understand why this place matters before seeing the AI-related spaces.

visitor_nodes.highlight: The proposal becomes useful, not only spectacular: a shaded walking edge, small food and repair services, seating, and visible wayfinding.
visitor_nodes.no_app_fallback: Prices, opening hours, and directions are printed on a shared physical board.
visitor_nodes.visitor_problem_solved: I need food, a seat, and a simple way to continue without losing the route.

visitor_nodes.highlight: A legible pause every 300–450 m combines shade, water, seating with backs and arms, drainage explanation, and a safe crossing.
visitor_nodes.no_app_fallback: The weather and route diversion board is updated by staff and readable from standing and seated height.
visitor_nodes.visitor_problem_solved: I need to rest, understand the weather, and decide whether to continue or shorten the route.

visitor_nodes.highlight: The visitor sees how AI is translated into everyday public service: accessible information, open demonstrations, and a real person who can explain limits.
visitor_nodes.no_app_fallback: The same demonstration is available as a physical flipbook, printed decision tree, or guided conversation.
visitor_nodes.visitor_problem_solved: I want to see something meaningful, not just a slogan or a screen.

visitor_nodes.highlight: Every route has an explicit human handover point for questions, accessibility needs, lost items, safety concerns, and turning back.
visitor_nodes.no_app_fallback: A numbered paper ticket links a question to a person and a response time; no personal profile is needed.
visitor_nodes.visitor_problem_solved: If the automated or digital service fails, I know exactly where a human can take over.

visitor_nodes.highlight: The most distinctive AI visit: three small, observable tests show robot yielding, service interoperability, and offline degradation with a safety steward.
visitor_nodes.no_app_fallback: Visitors can watch a fixed demonstration or read the test result without registering or being recorded.
visitor_nodes.visitor_problem_solved: I want to see a real innovation test while knowing what is simulated, optional, and safe.

visitor_nodes.highlight: A low-stimulation detour offers toilets, shade, a child-safe pause, and a quiet seating edge away from demonstrations.
visitor_nodes.no_app_fallback: A physical color band leads back to the main spine; children can follow landmarks instead of a phone map.
visitor_nodes.visitor_problem_solved: Different members of my group need different levels of stimulation and walking speed.

visitor_nodes.highlight: The visit closes with a choice: return along the green spine, take the short quiet loop, or record a paper feedback card.
visitor_nodes.no_app_fallback: A printed return strip shows distance bands and the next rest point; there is no forced digital check-out.
visitor_nodes.visitor_problem_solved: I know how to leave without retracing confusing crossings or depending on a live map.

routes.story: Arrive, understand the railway memory, experience everyday public space, see one meaningful AI demonstration, and return with a human fallback.
convenience: maximum one-way walking segment under 650 m
routes.rain_option: Use the covered NODE-02–NODE-06 sequence and replace the open garden pause with the courtyard demonstration.

routes.story: Read the past, observe daily life, compare community-scale AI with industry-scale testing, then decompress in a quiet garden before returning.
convenience: food and water on the spine
routes.rain_option: Keep the same sequence but use indoor/covered exhibits at NODE-03, NODE-06, and NODE-08; staff issue a shortened return card.

routes.name_en: Slow and Quiet: Accessible Experience Loop
routes.story: A shorter loop with predictable rest, low-stimulation edges, human guidance, and a clear escape to the arrival foyer.
routes.rain_option: Switch to the covered courtyard path and keep the same paper route color. Final slope, crossing, and accessible toilet details require specialist review.

service_standards.target: At every decision point, provide a large-print sign, a color band, a route number, and a landmark icon; digital directions are optional.
service_standards.verification: walk the route with first-time visitors and record wrong turns

service_standards.target: Provide a shaded rest/water opportunity every 300–450 m on the main route and 250–350 m on the slow/quiet route target.
service_standards.verification: measure the built route after official geometry and facility locations are confirmed

service_standards.target: A visible person or staffed contact point is reachable from each anchor; paper tickets and response-time commitments replace invisible digital queues.
service_standards.verification: mystery-visitor test for questions, lost items, safety, accessibility, and route change

service_standards.target: A visitor can complete the short route with printed information, physical signs, cash-compatible everyday services, and human assistance only.
service_standards.verification: run an offline/no-phone visitor test and publish failures plus repairs

service_standards.target: Rain, heat, fatigue, lost child, lost item, and service failure each have a visible short route and a human contact point.
service_standards.verification: tabletop exercise followed by controlled site test

visitor_personas.need: One coherent story and a route that fits two hours.
visitor_personas.design_response: NODE-02 route briefing, ROUTE-01, physical memory sequence, and a clear return point.

visitor_personas.need: Short attention cycles, toilets, food, safe pauses, and a way to split and reunite.
visitor_personas.design_response: NODE-04, NODE-09, family detour, landmark-based wayfinding, and no-road-crossing pause zones.

visitor_personas.name_zh: 银龄或行动较慢的游客
visitor_personas.need: Predictable rest, shade, seating with backs and arms, and a human who can change the route.
visitor_personas.design_response: ROUTE-03, NODE-05, NODE-07, and a paper distance band rather than a live map.

visitor_personas.name_zh: 无障碍与低数字技能游客
visitor_personas.name_en: Visitor with accessibility or low digital confidence
visitor_personas.need: No mandatory registration, clear physical information, and the ability to stop or ask for help.
visitor_personas.design_response: No-App Welcome Desk, tactile/large-print route strip, human takeover, and specialist accessibility testing before construction.

visitor_personas.need: A meaningful explanation of what is real, simulated, tested, and still pending.
visitor_personas.design_response: ROUTE-02, test result boards, visible safety boundaries, source notes, and explicit AI limits.

weather_and_safety: Rain: use the covered NODE-02–NODE-06 sequence and issue a paper short-route card.
Heat: prioritize shaded rest points, water, shorter loops, and a human recommendation to stop.
Fatigue: every route has a visible turn-back node; no visitor is penalized for leaving early.
Lost child or item: use the numbered human takeover station and paper log; do not require a personal profile.
AI or sensor failure: switch to fixed signs, paper boards, and a staffed explanation point.
Accessibility: all slopes, crossings, toilets, tactile cues, and emergency clearances remain subject to specialist and real-user testing.

evidence.review_limit: Route distance, travel time, facility spacing, slope, crossing safety, and operating hours are design targets until official geometry, engineering surveys, and user testing are available.
